history.period: Present structure 10th century; revered in the 7th-century Tevaram as a Paadal Petra Sthalam
history.summary: CSV TOWN FLAG: this temple is NOT in Tiruppur town - it is in THIRUMURUGANPOONDI, a panchayat town in Avinashi taluk, Tiruppur district, about 8-9 km from Tiruppur (and ~4 km from Avinashi). Documented with the corrected town. The Thirumuruganatheeswar Temple is a Shiva temple built in the Dravidian style, believed to be constructed during the Kongu Chola period in the 10th century. Legend: after destroying Soorapadma, Muruga was afflicted with the sin of mass killing; to absolve it he installed a Shiva linga here and worshipped it - hence the deity is 'Thirumuruganathaswamy', 'Master of Muruga'. The temple is a Paadal Petra Sthalam, revered in the 7th-century Tevaram by the Nayanmars. A granite wall encloses all the shrines; unusually, the temple has no rajagopuram (gateway tower). Four daily rituals are held; the Brahmotsavam in Maasi (for Sundarar) and Mahashivaratri are the most prominent festivals. It is one of the seven Siva sthalams of Kongu Nadu. It is maintained and administered by the Hindu Religious and Charitable Endowments Board (HR&CE) of Tamil Nadu; the temple website is thirumuruganpoonditemple.tnhrce.in.

name: Sri Tirumuruganathaswamy Temple
town: Thirumuruganpoondi (CSV town 'Tiruppur' is WRONG - the temple is in Thirumuruganpoondi town, ~8-9 km from Tiruppur)
town_description: Thirumuruganpoondi is a panchayat town in Avinashi taluk of Tiruppur district, Tamil Nadu (2011 population ~31,500; area 14.5 sq km). Nearest town is Tiruppur (~8-9 km); Avinashi is ~4 km; Coimbatore is ~56 km.
tradition: Hinduism (Shaivism; Paadal Petra Sthalam of the Nayanmars)

travel.railway: Tiruppur railway station - about 8 km; Vanjipalaiyam - about 6 km.
travel.road: On the road between Tiruppur and Avinashi; town buses and private buses serve Thirumuruganpoondi.
